item.title: Jerry Jones on Joey Porter Jr. trade: "It's important to think big"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Steelers decided to move on from cornerback Joey Porter Jr.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers decided to move on from cornerback Joey Porter Jr. The Cowboys were ready to pounce.

"It’s important to think big," Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, "and this is over in that big thought area about what we can do to help our defense."

As to whether other moves will be made this year, Jones said "it's always fluid" and "you can't sit still."

"If you look at the overall picture, I frankly decided a couple of years ago to get in the business of reworking what we are defensively," Jones said.

The Porter trade is about winning now. The question is whether one player will make a big difference. The Cowboys have seen their cornerback play dip since trading linebacker Micah Parsons, and it's not a coincidence. It's easier to cover receivers if the quarterback is rushing to throw — or not throwing at all.

Porter isn't Deion Sanders. (Then again, no one is.) The issue in Pittsburgh was that the two sides had a dramatically different viewpoint as to his value. And the eventual price that Cowboys paid (a sixih-round pick in 2027 and a second-round pick in 2028, with the possibility of a third-round compensatory pick in 2028 if he leave in free agency after this season) reflects the Steelers' assessment of Porter as a player.

Porter's value to the Cowboys remains to be seen. But all signs are pointing to Porter getting his first chance to show what he can do for his new team on Sunday.

item.title: Liam Coen on Travis Hunter's usage: "He cares about winning"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Questions have persisted regarding whether the Jaguars are getting the most out of cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter, the second overall pick in the 2025 draft.
item.content:encoded:
Questions have persisted regarding whether the Jaguars are getting the most out of cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter, the second overall pick in the 2025 draft. Coach Liam Coen addressed the situation in simple terms on Friday.

"He cares about winning," Coen said, "That's what he cares about. Like, and all the other stuff, the reps, where we picked him, does that — I don't give two Fs about value. And neither does he. We care about winning. And that's it."

That's not what Hunter said in an August appearance on The Pivot podcast. He said he wants to play both sides of the ball, on a full-time basis.

“If I’m trying to be the best — how are you gonna be the best, if you ain’t trying to be the best?" Hunter said at the time. "If you ain’t trying to compete and do the best to be the best? So my main focus is be the best. So I’m gonna do everything I can do to be the best. I don’t want to be the best at one position. There’s a lot of people that’s the best at one position. Ain’t nobody yet been the best at both, full-time. . . .

"I cannot sit on the sideline. I don’t think nobody’s noticed that yet. I hate the sidelines. I do not wanna sit there. I can’t sit there and just watch football. I’ve got to be on the field.”

The fact that the Jaguars are winning makes it harder for Hunter to gripe about his usage, which is increasing on the defensive side of the ball but which continues to be cameo appearances, at best, on offense. But he's on the record with his wishes.

And, yes, it's fair to ask about value. Especially given the glowing remarks G.M. James Gladstone made after the Jaguars traded up from No. 5 to No. 2 to get him.

“This is something I’m uniquely positioned to navigate," Gladstone said in April 2025. "We ended up bringing Travis Hunter to Jacksonville, and with that, he is somebody who is deserving of a first-round draft pick as a wide receiver, and he is worthy of a first-round draft pick as a corner. Certainly, look forward to each of those elements showing themselves over the next few years while he is under his rookie contract."

While the Jaguars have emerged as an elite team, the stated vision for Hunter has yet to come to fruition. And it seems that no one wants that to happen more than him.

item.title: Rams don't have a timeline on Myles Garrett's return
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Despite a report that Rams defensive end Myles Garrett would miss about six weeks with his knee injury, head coach Sean McVay says the team isn't working on a timeline that specific.
item.content:encoded:
Despite a report that Rams defensive end Myles Garrett would miss about six weeks with his knee injury, head coach Sean McVay says the team isn't working on a timeline that specific.

Asked how Garrett is doing after knee surgery, McVay said Garrett is doing well but told reporters the team does not have any time frame for when he will actually be back on the field.

"Myles is good. I've seen him in there, he physically looks good," McVay said. "He's got a good look in his eye. It's been good having him in and out of a lot of the meetings while he's attacking his rehab. He's making good progress, but as far as a specific timeline, I'm not ready to give you guys that. As soon as I have those things I'll give you guys updates."

After sitting out practice with a knee injury in training camp and struggling to play on his injured knee in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers, Garrett had surgery and was placed on injured reserve. By rule, players on injured reserve have to miss at least four weeks, but it appears that Garrett will be out longer than that. How much longer, the Rams still don't know.

item.title: Maxx Crosby: Vegas is a different type of city, we have to earn home-field advantage
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "We're new to this city and we have to win. The fans come out, they want to see a winner. We have to earn that," Crosby said.
item.content:encoded:
The Raiders haven't had a lot of success since moving to Las Vegas in 2020, but things may be changing. The Raiders are 3-0, on Sunday they host the 3-0 Chiefs, and Maxx Crosby says now is the time to show what kind of home-field advantage Allegiant Stadium can provide.

Crosby said that unlike Oakland and Los Angeles, where the rabid fans of the Black Hole were legendary, Vegas is a city where the Raiders are going to need to develop a fan base that isn't yet so invested in the team.

"We’re gonna need the fans at full effect, and that's all season," Crosby said. "We have to earn our stadium, and having the fans here. In Oakland it's built in, fans are going to show up, it's going to be Silver and Black. L.A. is the same thing. But Vegas is a different type of city. We're new to this city and we have to win. The fans come out, they want to see a winner. We have to earn that."

Crosby thinks winning comes first and the home-field advantage follows.

"We take it one day at a time and keep earning the respect, and love and passion for the fans. We know the fans have it, to fill that stadium every Sunday with Silver and Black, we've got to continue winning and keep putting a great product out there for the fans," Crosby said.

If the Raiders beat the Chiefs on Sunday, a whole lot of Las Vegas fans will be buying in.

item.title: Sean McVay: I don't like it that the Rams are 1-2, but we grow through adversity
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "It's a challenge for me: What kind of leader do I want to be for this group?" McVay said.
item.content:encoded:
Rams coach Sean McVay isn't happy with his team's 1-2 start this season, but he isn't losing confidence in the long-term plan, and he even thinks the Rams might be better in January for what they went through in September.

"Do I love the fact that we've played three games and came up short in a couple of them? No, of course not," McVay said. "But what I also know is this: There's been other moments that it seems like you're in some storms, but this too shall pass, and let's do the next right thing. Let's lean in. What kind of lens do we want to see this through? Do we want to see this as, this is happening to me or for me, and how can I learn from it, how can I grow? It's a challenge for me: What kind of leader do I want to be for this group?"

McVay said he believes in growing through adversity, even if it doesn't feel good at the time.

"Do I want to go through that adversity? No, but this is what we're going through," McVay said. "That's what makes it meaningful. When things come easy, sometimes when you have success you become less resilient. I do not like it but I do know that's where the real growth occurs."

McVay said he thinks when this season is over, his team might be more proud of its accomplishments because of the early struggles.

"Sometimes it doesn't go down for you and I always think about the people I respect the most are the ones that handle the tough times the best," McVay said. "Tough times don't last. Tough people do. The most growth that's ever occurred for me by far is when we've been in those adverse moments when you don't like it when you're in them, but then you look back and say you're proud of the person you became from them."

Up next for the Rams is a game at Philadelphia on Sunday, and McVay acknowledged his own struggles against the Eagles.

"I'm excited to swing and compete again with this group. This story is not yet written. There are people who feel otherwise, but we've got a lot of ball ahead of us," McVay said. "We've got a great challenge. This is an excellent place to play at, great fan base. We're not going to run away from that we haven't gotten the results when we've gone up there. Last year was a gut-wrenching one but I'm not afraid to put it out there again."

For the Rams, who were heavy preseason favorites to win the Super Bowl, falling to 1-3 would be a massive letdown. But McVay continues to believe that his team won't stay down.

item.title: YouTube believes NFL could "deconstruct" Sunday Ticket in next broadcast deals
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Come 2030, out-of-market games could be seen without plunking down an extra $400.
item.content:encoded:
The next wave of NFL broadcast deals could include plenty of changes. One change could be the end of the out-of-market package of games.

Via Alex Sherman of CNBC, YouTube believes that the NFL could “deconstruct” Sunday Ticket.

The league first launched Sunday Ticket in 1994, marketing it as a way for fans to watch games not televised in the markets where they reside. DirecTV owned the package for years, before YouTube acquired the rights in 2023.

The current Sunday Ticket deal with YouTube, for which the company pays $2 billion per year, remains the subject of a federal class action that is pending on appeal in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, The case could still result in a massive liability for the NFL (in excess of $14 billion). It also could generate a court order compelling the NFL to end the longstanding device for allowing fans to watch all games played in the Sunday afternoon windows.

The NFL lost at trial in 2024. The jury found that the NFL's pricing of the package, which was intended to be high enough to persuade many viewers to choose to watch the CBS and Fox games available in their local markets, violated the antitrust laws.

The judge didn't throw out the entire verdict; he dismissed the damages award. The finding of an antitrust violation remains in place — and it continues.

At some point, there likely will be a reckoning. And the league has already explored the possibility of making the games available through other platforms, simulating a college football viewing experience that has a wide variety of games on various cable and broadcast platforms.

Quite possibly, the league could make as much or more money by selling in-market games to a pair of broadcast networks, with the out-of-market games sprinkled throughout the various other channels on the dial.

Regardless of the revenue potential, the league will have no choice, if a court compels them to dismantle Sunday Ticket. And it would allow fans to watch games on networks to which they already have access, without paying nearly $400 per year for it.

Ditching Sunday Ticket would also address concerns that the league has devalued it by putting more and more games into non-Sunday windows. And it would give the NFL the freedom to more aggressively schedule games for Wednesday nights and, eventually, Tuesday nights.

item.title: Quarterbacks who didn't start in Week 1 are 6-0
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: It's the year of the backup quarterback, so far.
item.content:encoded:
It's the year of the backup quarterback, so far.

Through three weeks, six quarterbacks who didn't start in Week 1 have since started six games. They're collectively 6-0.

Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz started and won at Chicago in Week 2. Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock started and won at Arizona in Week 2. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. started and won at Green Bay in Week 3. Giants quarterback Jameis Winston started and won vs. the Titans in Week 3. Washington quarterback Marcus Mariota started and won vs. the Seahawks in Week 6. And Bears quarterback Case Keenum started and won vs. the Eagles in Week 3.

In Week 4, two more quarterbacks who didn't start in Week 1 are expected to start their first games of the season: Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent vs. the Jets and Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels vs. the Packers.

The situation shows the importance of having two, if not three, quarterbacks who can be counted on to play, and play well. A game here or a game there in the absence of the starting quarterback could eventually make the difference between making the playoffs or missing the bus.

item.title: Sean McVay is 0-4 against Nick Sirianni
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Rams coach Sean McVay has had tremendous success since becoming a head coach in 2017.
item.content:encoded:
Rams coach Sean McVay has had tremendous success since becoming a head coach in 2017. Against one specific coach, McVay has struggled.

Via NBC Sports research, McVay has an 0-4 record against Eagles coach Nick Sirianni.

McVay gets his next chance to get his first win over Sirianni on Sunday in Philadelphia. The 1-2 Rams desperately need to avoid falling to 1-3.

In 2023, the Eagles and Sirianni beat the Rams and McVay in L.A., 23-14. The next year, the Eagles won again in L.A., 37-20.

In the 2024 playoffs, the Eagles escaped an upset bid in the divisional round, 28-22. Last season, a blocked field goal in the final seconds (returned for a touchdown) gave the Eagles a 33-26 win.

Overall, McVay is 1-6 against the Eagles. And Philly has won 10 of the last 11 games played between the two teams.

The Rams are nevertheless favored by 3.5 points over the Eagles. The game starts at 1:00 p.m. ET on Sunday.

item.title: Five teams face an 0-4 start — and only one 0-4 team has ever made the playoffs
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Week 4 is here, and five teams are still looking for their first victory of 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Week 4 is here, and five teams are still looking for their first victory of 2026.

The Dolphins, Texans, Titans, Chargers, and Buccaneers are all 0-3. Only seven teams (most recently, the 2025 Texans) have made the playoffs after an 0-3 start.

None of the five teams play each other this weekend, which means all five could still be winless come Monday. Any that land at 0-4 will be facing a steep climb to the postseason.

Only one team in NFL history has qualified for the playoffs after starting 0-4. In 1992, the Chargers under first-year coach Bobby Ross turned it around and secured the AFC West crown. The Chargers won 11 of their 12 final games of the season.

The Chargers advanced through the wild-card round with a 17-0 win over the Chiefs, who had swept the Chargers during the regular season. The next week, the Dolphins eliminated the Chargers with a 31-0 blowout.

With 17 games and seven playoff spots per conference, it's easier than ever for a team to turn it around after an 0-4 start. Still, many 0-4 teams start that way for a reason; they're not very good. The 1992 Chargers were much better than their early-season record indicated, and they made it all the way to the final eight.

item.title: New Bears stadium in Illinois could be publicly owned
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Bears claim to be focused on building a new stadium in Indiana.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears claim to be focused on building a new stadium in Indiana. And yet they're still talking to Illinois.

Via Danny Ecker of Crain's Chicago Business, the possible construction in Arlington Heights could entail a publicly-owned venue.

Per the report, recent discussions between the Bears and Illinois officials have focused on a public model. Thursday's meeting between, Commissioner Roger Goodell, Bears minority owner Pat Ryan, Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, and state legislative leaders, has renewed hope that the Bears won't cross the border for their next home.

Ecker also points out that Bears president and CEO Kevin Warren and primary owner George McCaskey were "notably absent" from Thursday's meeting.

Public ownership would solve the property-tax question that has stalled the team's ability to convert the Arlington Park site, which the Bears own, into a new stadium.

The goal is to craft legislation that would pass both houses of the Illinois Legislature.

The Bears originally intended to own, and to privately finance, the new stadium. That strategy hasn't gained sufficient footing. The leverage that comes from the Indiana option has spurred the powers-that-be in Illinois to explore a different strategy that would keep the team from leaving the state.

The best outcome would be, in our view, a new stadium in Chicago. If that's not doable, it's far better for the Bears to stay in Illinois than to move to another state.

Still, the Indiana option has always seemed to be aimed at getting the attention of Illinois. That apparently has worked. The next question is whether they can get a deal done to build a new stadium in Illinois.

Until then, the Bears will continue to play at Soldier Field. Enjoy the open-air experience while it lasts.

item.title: Vinod Khosla on a potential Seahawks move: "Never say never"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: New owner keeps saying things that won't make the fan base happy.
item.content:encoded:
Q: What's the best way to get the Seahawks' fan base to forget that the new owner is a Steelers fan who still watches all of their games?

A: Fail to unequivocally rule out the possibility of moving the team to a new city.

"I will never say never," new owner Vinod Khosla told Dan Primack of Axios. "Will this team be in Seattle 500 years from now? But I have no current plans to change anything about the team, including the coach, president, operation or Lumen Field. It all functions well."

The 500-year question is far less relevant than the six-year question. The team's lease at Lumen Field expires in 2032.

Khosla may simply be playing the game of stadium politics. In order to get someone else to pay for major renovations or a new stadium, leverage must exist. If nothing else, "never say never" helps set the stage for an infusion of significant taxpayer money.

Besides, Khosla is still learning the ropes of being an owner.

"Three months ago I wasn't even thinking about buying an NFL team," Khosla said. "Now I ended up with a Super Bowl-winning team with one of the most amazing fan bases. But I know very little about running a team. I don't think I'll do anything but learn for a while."

One thing Khosla may realize the hard way is a lesson that plenty of other anonymous billionaires turned NFL owners have learned: The only thing better than being rich and famous is being rich.

Khosla's comments will make the fan base leery about the future. How can they not be? But they don't deserve to be caught in the crossfire of the billion-dollar gamesmanship over who'll pay for the next Seahawks stadium.

item.title: NFL fines Quinn Meinerz $14,926 for a celebratory dice roll
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Broncos right guard Quinn Meinerz celebrated with Jaylen Waddle after the wide receiver's 2-point conversion on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos right guard Quinn Meinerz celebrated with Jaylen Waddle after the wide receiver's 2-point conversion on Sunday. He playfully "waddled" over to offer his congratulations, and the teammates then pantomimed a dice roll.

“I got fined,’’ Meinerz told Mike Klis of 9News. “We were playing Yahtzee. They didn’t like we were playing Yahtzee.”

In 2017, the NFL announced that it had no problem with celebratory dice rolls. A spokesperson at the time said the league "isn't in a place to determine" whether players were referring to Yahtzee or backgammon.

The league fined Meinerz $14,926 for what the league deemed an illegal celebration. It seems likely the NFL fined Waddle the same amount.

Meinerz said he will appeal.

After the Broncos' second 2-point conversion, Meinerz lifted Pat Bryant II off the ground with a two-arm, elbow-locked shiver.

“It’s fun to be back to who I am and I can breathe. I can see, I’m feeling good about life and where things are at,’’ Meinerz said. “So when I have the opportunity to use more of that energy to go celebrate with my teammates, why not? It’s hard to score, have fun with it.”

item.title: Chiefs DB Chamarri Conner set to make his season debut
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Chiefs defensive back Chamarri Conner is set to make his 2026 debut on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs defensive back Chamarri Conner is set to make his 2026 debut on Sunday.

Conner missed the first three games with a knee injury.

He led the team in defensive snap percentage last season and is a favorite of defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo. Conner can play nickel or safety.

“It seems like every year he’s been here — and we’ve done cut-ups at the end of the season and we’re looking through the film — 27 keeps showing up, making plays,” Spagnuolo said, via Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star. “Hopefully, we can get him back there doing that. I think he’s a really good tackler and a good football player.

“We’ll fit him in there, whether it’s a safety or nickel in certain packages. And I like having him on the field, and I’m hoping we get him for this game.”

Jaden Hicks and Alohi Gilman have started at safety in Conner's absence, and Hicks has played every snap.

Starting left tackle Josh Simmons will miss his fourth consecutive game to start the season. He has a bulging disc in his lower back.

Undrafted rookie Khalil Benson has started in Simmons' stead.

item.title: Keenan Allen misses Friday's practice, questionable to play Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Colts did not rule out any players for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London, but they do have a pair of wide receivers listed as questionable.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts did not rule out any players for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London, but they do have a pair of wide receivers listed as questionable.

Keenan Allen was listed as a non-participant in Friday's practice due to a groin injury. Allen was a limited participant in the team's first two practices of the week.

Ashton Dulin missed the last two games with an ankle injury and did not practice on Wednesday, but has been a full participant in the last two practices.

item.title: Mike Evans is going to try to play through his injured ribs
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Broncos after a limited practice Friday.
item.content:encoded:
49ers wide receiver Mike Evans is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Broncos after a limited practice Friday. He is going to try to play with a built-in compression shirt with padding in it to protect his injured ribs.

Coach Kyle Shanahan called Evans a "game-time decision."

"I'm going to do my best [to play]," Evans said, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com.

He has previously played through something similar.

Evans said he isn't certain exactly when he injured his ribs, but it didn't feel good.

"That shit hurt bad," Evans said. "It was like non-contact. It might have happened before, but when I ran a route, and I turned, I just felt it, like, 'Ah!' Felt like somebody stabbed me in my chest.

"But it's cool. The training staff and doctors did a good job of getting me off the field and making sure I was good."

Shanahan broke his ribs in a car wreck this summer, so he sympathizes with Evans.

"Mine are good now, but it's been two months, and I would not be questionable," Shanahan said. "I would be out, without a doubt. But he's definitely a lot tougher than me, so hopefully we've got a shot."

The 49ers ruled out defensive linemen Nick Bosa (knee/calf), James Thompson Jr. (ankle) and Mykel Williams (knee).

Left tackle Trent Williams (neck) does not have an injury designation.

Defensive end Keion White (hamstring), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (quad) and linebacker Jaden Dugger (shoulder) are questionable. Dugger was a new addition to the injury report Friday.

item.title: Stephen Jones: Steelers' initial asking price for Joey Porter Jr. was "a little hefty"
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Cowboys Executive V.P.
item.content:encoded:
Cowboys Executive V.P. Stephen Jones says the team spent significant time negotiating a trade with the Steelers for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. that made sense for the Cowboys — and made the trade only after the Steelers' price came down.

Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that what the Steelers were initially asking for was more than the Cowboys were willing to give up, but they eventually got the Steelers to lower the price to a 2027 sixth-round pick and 2028 second-round pick.

"Early on the price was a little hefty for us, then it got to a point where we could deal with it," Jones said.

Jones said the Cowboys know there's a chance Porter will leave in free agency after this season, but they think if he does, they'll get a 2028 compensatory pick that largely makes up for losing the 2028 second-round pick.

"We had to have that trade make sense if Joey left after this year," Jones said. "That's why the 2 in '28 matches up with a compensatory pick. If he did leave we'd probably get a 3 or a 4 for him and get that back for Joey in '28 when that 2 is in place. So it made a lot of sense. It protected us."

Even if Porter proves to be only a rental for the rest of this season before going elsewhere, Jones thinks the price was right, once the Steelers lowered it.

item.title: NFL reminds teams that conversations on officiating are "confidential"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL routinely communicates with teams regarding concerns arising from calls made and not made in the most recent games.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL routinely communicates with teams regarding concerns arising from calls made and not made in the most recent games. The league, with some express exceptions, does not want the teams talking publicly about the contents of the conversations.

On Friday, the NFL sent a memo reminding all teams that such communications are "confidential," and not for external disclosure.

The memo is an obvious response to Rams coach Sean McVay's decision to spill the beans on his discussions with the league regarding the controversial defensive pass interference call at the end of Sunday night's game against the Broncos. While it's unknown whether McVay was fined for the infraction, the memo makes clear that the league doesn't want its coaches flipping the lid on Pandora’s box.

As noted yesterday, what will the league do if it admits that such an important mistake (we still don't think it was a mistake) changed the outcome of a game? Refund all wagers on the Rams? Los Angeles closed as a 0.5-point favorite. All moneyline and spread wagers on the Rams that lost were, based on that admission, winners.

It's just a matter of time before someone files a nationwide class action arising from losses that should have been wins due to avoidable officiating errors. The NFL's too-cozy relationship with gambling makes it inevitable.

Having one of the coaches hold up the smoking gun and wave it around for all to see makes it easy.

item.title: CBS, Tony Romo undoubtedly negotiated a contract settlement
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Friday's announcement that CBS and No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo have "mutually agreed to part ways" hardly means that the separation was a joint decision.
item.content:encoded:
Friday's announcement that CBS and No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo have "mutually agreed to part ways" hardly means that the separation was a joint decision. Romo had vowed to return to CBS; CBS clearly did not want him back.

The mutual agreement comes from the paperwork. With Romo owed $72 million over four years, ending the relationship meant reaching an agreement on how much he'll be paid to walk away.

Andrew Marchand of The Athletic writes that "CBS preferred to eat a good portion of the remaining money" to fighting with Romo over how much he'd get. Marchand notes that the "exact figure" is "unknown." As Marchand surmises, the fact that the situation was resolved without full-blown litigation or arbitration means it was not insignificant.

Our guess (and it's just a guess) is that Romo will get anywhere from half to two-thirds of the money — $36 million to $48 million. While CBS may have had a silver bullet in the contract allowing for termination without pay for violation of a broad and vague "morals clause," it would have been difficult to make it stick based solely on an OWI arrest and ensuing no-contest plea.

And the simple reality is that CBS used the situation as a way to pull the plug. If CBS felt the same way about Romo as it did when he signed his latest contract, they would have found a way to excuse the situation and move on. He was already on thin ice at CBS, based in incessant criticisms of his performances. The OWI arrest was tantamount to Romo jumping up and down on it.

Romo still gets a sizable portion of the money. But he doesn't get all of it, and he also loses the status and the profile that comes with being the top NFL analyst at one of the few networks that televise NFL games watched by millions every week.
